page_title: Writing one sentence per line | Derek Sivers

summary.title: Writing one sentence per line
summary.one_liner: Writing each sentence on its own line, for your own eyes only, helps you judge, reorder, and tighten your sentences.
takeaways: Put each sentence on its own line while drafting; it's for your eyes only, not for publishing.
Seeing sentences separately makes it easier to spot and delete sentences that don't need to exist.
Vertical layout helps you vary sentence length and move your best sentences to the start or end of a paragraph.
Check the first and last word of each line: cut weak openers like 'I think' and start with strong subjects and verbs.
summary.summary: Derek Sivers, who says he has practiced this for twenty years, recommends writing one sentence per line as a private drafting method. The short page gives four reasons: judging each sentence on its own, varying sentence length, rearranging sentences more easily, and examining first and last words. It notes that HTML or Markdown would merge the lines into one paragraph, so the format is for drafting only. The page is a brief opinion piece with no code or examples beyond the layout itself.
